settings.section_text:
You've done the dance. Read every label twice. Googled ingredients you can't pronounce. Watched someone across the table eat something you used to love and thought,"must be nice."

FireCreek meat sticks are 100% gluten free across every flavor we make. Including our Teriyaki, which, yes, is actually gluten free. No soy sauce with hidden wheat. No "processed in a facility" fine print. Just real meat, clean seasoning, and protein you can eat without a second thought.

settings.section_caption: All four flavors · Zero gluten · No asterisks

settings.grid_box_text:
Most teriyaki-flavored meat sticks and jerky contain soy sauce. Standard soy sauce is brewed with wheat. That means most "teriyaki" products contain gluten — even when nothing else in the ingredient list raises a flag.

Some brands slap "natural flavors" on the label and hope you don't dig deeper. If you've been gluten free long enough, you've learned not to trust teriyaki anything. We get it.

FireCreek Teriyaki is built differently. Ryan, a third generation butcher, has a son with extreme food sensitivities, including gluten, and his goal was to create a great tasting snack that was healthy, which his son could eat without issue. This is a core part of FireCreek Snacks meat sticks. 

From day one, every flavor we developed was designed to be gluten free from the ground up — including the one that most brands can't figure out.

settings.heading: Are these certified gluten-free?
settings.row_content: Not yet. We don't have third-party GFCO certification at this point. What we do have: every ingredient we use is verified gluten free at the sourcing level, our Teriyaki uses a gluten free soy alternative instead of standard soy sauce, and we're transparent about everything that goes into our sticks (scroll up, we listed it all). Certification is on our radar, but we'd rather be honest about where we are than slap a logo on the package we haven't earned yet.

settings.heading: I have celiac disease. Is this safe for me?
settings.row_content: We take this seriously. Our products are made with 100% gluten free ingredients and our Teriyaki specifically avoids standard soy sauce, the most common hidden gluten source in this flavor category. That said, we are not currently third-party certified, and we want you to make the call that's right for your body and your comfort level. Want to know more about our sourcing or production process? Email us and we'll give you specifics. No runaround, no form letter.

settings.heading: What makes the Teriyaki gluten-free when most are not?
settings.row_content: Standard teriyaki sauce uses soy sauce, which is typically brewed with wheat. That's why most teriyaki-flavored snacks contain gluten even when the rest of the product is clean. We use a gluten free soy alternative in our Teriyaki seasoning. It's not an afterthought or a reformulation — we built every flavor, including Teriyaki, to be gluten free from day one.

settings.heading: What about cross-contamination?
settings.row_content: Our products are made with gluten free ingredients throughout our process. We don't use wheat, barley, rye, or any gluten-containing grains in any of our products. If you have specific questions about our facility or production lines, reach out to us directly and we'll walk you through it. We'd rather over-share than leave you guessing.

settings.heading: How is this different from other "gluten-free" meat sticks?
settings.row_content: Most meat sticks that claim gluten free are just... regular meat sticks that happen to not have wheat in them. They're not built for people who actually live gluten free. We are. That means no soy sauce with wheat in the Teriyaki. No malt extract hiding in the seasoning. No "natural flavors" as a catch-all. We designed every flavor for people who read ingredient lists like legal documents, because we know you do.

settings.heading: Do they actually taste good, or is it a "good for being gluten-free"?
settings.row_content: We'll let you judge, but here's the tell: most of our customers aren't gluten free. They just like meat sticks. The fact that they're GF is a bonus, not the reason people buy them. When a product is only good "for gluten free," that means it's not actually good. FireCreek is good, period. The GF part is just how it's built.
